claim: For every integer base \(b\ge2\), if \(a,c\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(\gcd(a,b)=\gcd(c,b)=1\) and \(S_b(an)=S_b(cn)\) for every \(n\ge1\), then \(a=c\). Consequently, for every prime \(p\), \(S_p(an)=S_p(cn)\) for all \(n\ge1\) if and only if \(a/p^{\nu_p(a)}=c/p^{\nu_p(c)}\), equivalently \(a/c\in p^{\mathbb Z}\). Thus base-shift symmetry is the only obstruction in prime bases, while coprime multipliers are rigid in every base.
integrity: The proof is symbolic. The repeated-block construction, bounded-borrow lemma, and prime-base reduction are stated explicitly; computational checks are separated from proof.
scientific_limitations: For composite bases, arbitrary multipliers sharing factors with the base are not classified; the theorem proves coprime rigidity.
The prime-base classification is complete for the first digit-sum iterate only; no claim is made about higher iterates of the digit-sum map.
Finite computation is regression evidence only and is not used as an infinite proof.
title: Coprime rigidity and exact prime-base collisions for digit sums
